name: Republic of Peru

areaKm2.note: asOf 2024. Surface area 1,285,216 km2 (AG.SRF.TOTL.K2); low is land area 1,280,000 km2 (AG.LND.TOTL.K2).

population.note: asOf 2025 (World Bank SP.POP.TOTL 34,576,665). Low/high +/-1% for 2026 change and census revision. Everything inside ne:PER.

activePersonnel.note: IISS Military Balance 2026 p.439 as quoted: 81,000 active (excludes 77,000 paramilitary National Police). CIA Factbook 2025: ~85,000 (50,000 Army, 25,000 Navy, 10,000 Air Force).

trainedReserves.note: IISS Military Balance 2026: 188,000 reserves. Low is an educated figure for those realistically callable within 30 days.

supportPersonnel.note: Active 81,000 (IISS 2026) minus infantry P roles (3,000 + 25,000). Covers navy (25,988 active per Peruvian Navy article, minus marines in P roles), air force, crews, logistics, staff.

mobilizationRatio.note: Analogy to Andean conscript armies (1995 Cenepa war mobilization was limited); large IISS reserve (188,000) but little stored modern equipment. Educated judgement.

count.note: Educated guess. Mechanized infantry on M113, UR-416 and Fiat 6614. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_equipment_of_the_Peruvian_Army)

training.note: Rubric 0.5: voluntary military service (conscription suspended 1999), counter-terror experience in VRAEM, aging equipment limits training.

count.note: Educated guess. Jungle, mountain, airborne/commando battalions and ~4,000 marines. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_equipment_of_the_Peruvian_Army)

quality.note: Rubric 0.5 band minus: mixed small arms (Galil ACE, AKM, FAL), Spike/Kornet ATGMs.

training.note: Rubric 0.5: voluntary military service (conscription suspended 1999), counter-terror experience in VRAEM, aging equipment limits training.

count.note: Equipment list (IISS Military Balance 2024 p.448 as cited): T-55 ~280 incl. 75+ in store (low ~165-205 active) + AMX-13 ~108 light tanks (high). K2 Black Panther (54) contracted Nov 2024, none delivered; contract status uncertain (Oct 2026).

training.note: Rubric 0.5: voluntary military service (conscription suspended 1999), counter-terror experience in VRAEM, aging equipment limits training.

count.note: IISS 2024 via equipment list: BRDM-2 ~30 + Fiat 6616 ~15 + M9A1 ~50 + UR-416 ~150 + Fiat 6614 ~25 + M113A1 ~120 = 390. K808 (141) contracted but may be cancelled.

training.note: Rubric 0.5: voluntary military service (conscription suspended 1999), counter-terror experience in VRAEM, aging equipment limits training.

count.note: IISS 2024 via equipment list: M109A2 ~12 + M101 ~44 + M2A1 ~24 + M-56 ~60 + Model 56 ~24 + D-30 ~36 + M-46 ~36 + M114 ~36 + Model 50 ~30 + BM-21 ~22 + Type-90B ~27 = 351 (mortars excluded).

quality.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: mostly towed Cold War guns.

training.note: Rubric 0.5: voluntary military service (conscription suspended 1999), counter-terror experience in VRAEM, aging equipment limits training.

count.note: Peruvian Air Force inventory: Mirage 2000P 9 + 2000DP 2 + MiG-29SMP/UBP 6 = 17. F-16 Block 70 (12 ordered of 24 planned) not delivered; KC-135 part of the package halted by the president (Apr 2026).

Air Force: Bell 412 2 + Bell 212 1 + Mi-8 1 + Mi-17/171 10 + Mi-35 18 + Bo 105 2 + SH-2G 5 = 39 (FAP article); Army: Mi-8/17/171 ~43 + AW109 1 + Mi-2 1 + Enstrom/R44 4 = ~49 (Army equipment list, World Air Forces 2024); Navy ~12 (SH-3D, AB-212/412; educated). Total ~100.
Air Force: 6 domestically built reconnaissance UAVs (FAP article); Navy small systems (educated).
Peruvian Navy article: Carvajal-class 3 + Lupo-class 4 = 7 guided-missile frigates (Aguirre in sea trials after overhaul).

quality.note: Rubric 0.5 band minus: 1970s-80s Lupo design, partly upgraded with local CMS and Kronos radar.

count.note: Peruvian Navy article: PR-72P/Pohang missile corvettes 8 + offshore patrol vessels 13 (incl. ex-Carvajal operated by Coast Guard) + Makassar LPD 2 + LST 1 = 24 (low); fleet box lists 34 patrol ships (high side).
Peruvian Navy article: Type 209/1200 4 (Antofagasta in upgrade) + Type 209/1100 2 = 6 boats, 5 in service.

training.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: largest submarine force on the South American Pacific coast.

count.note: IISS 2024 via equipment list: ZSU-23-4 ~35 + ZU-23-2 ~130 guns and Igla/Strela MANPADS; Air Force Pechora sites not itemised. ~20 batteries, educated conversion.

commandQuality.note: Rubric 0.5: competent staff (CAEN, ESGE), Cenepa 1995 experience; political instability (frequent presidential changes) disrupts procurement.

cohesion.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: professional cadre, strong service identity (navy especially).

weapons.note: Between anchor 8 and 9: Kornet/Spike ATGMs, Exocet/Otomat, R-27/Super 530D; few precision munitions.

armor.note: Anchor 8: T-55 without composite armour; K2 not delivered.

ships.note: Below anchor 9: upgraded Lupo/Type 209, modern LPDs.

fortification.note: Anchor 8-9: southern frontier positions (Tacna), little air defence.

logistics.note: Between anchor 8 and 9: C-27J, Twin Otter airlift; Andes and Amazon depend on air and river transport.

communications.note: Below anchor 9: limited data links; no military satellite.

isr.note: Below anchor 9: PeruSAT-1 Earth-observation satellite, small UAV fleet.

air.note: Below anchor 9: Mirage 2000P and MiG-29SMP; F-16 Block 70 not delivered.

cyber.note: Below anchor 9-10: Joint Command cyber defence unit, small.

gdpPerCapita.note: asOf 2025. Rebased GDP 445,047,988,943 / population 34,576,665 = 12,871 2011 int$. Range +/-10%. Corrected 2026-10-29: values x1.0376 because the rebase factor was an arithmetic error (0.8005); the right factor is 0.8306 (FRED GDPDEF, 2017=100: 2011 91.478 / 2021 110.130). Figures quoted above are before the correction.

gdp.note: asOf 2025. World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD (constant 2021 int$) 555,962,509,610 x 0.8005 (US GDP deflator 2011/2021) = 445,047,988,943 2011 int$. Range +/-10% for PPP benchmark uncertainty and the relative-price drift the rebase ignores. Series: https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/PER/indicator/NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD?format=json Corrected 2026-10-29: values x1.0376 because the rebase factor was an arithmetic error (0.8005); the right factor is 0.8306 (FRED GDPDEF, 2017=100: 2011 91.478 / 2021 110.130). Figures quoted above are before the correction.

milSpendShare.note: SIPRI via World Bank: 0.81% of GDP in 2025. CIA Factbook 0.8% (2024), 1.1% (2021-22).

industrialShare.note: asOf 2024: industry incl. construction 34.32% of GDP (NV.IND.TOTL.ZS). Mining (copper, gold, zinc) dominant.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Exports fruit/vegetables (avocados, blueberries, asparagus) and fishmeal but imports cereals; not computed from FAO balance sheets.

annualCohort.note: asOf 2025. Males reaching military age per year = male population 17,193,234 (SP.POP.TOTL.MA.IN) x share of males aged 15-19 8.525% (SP.POP.1519.MA.5Y) / 5 = 293,150. Males only (conscript-pool convention); about double if women are counted. Range +/-10%.

ships_minor.note: Educated guess. SIMA Callao/Chimbote builds patrol vessels and LPDs (Makassar class under licence). (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peruvian_Navy)

roadKm.note: CIA World Factbook as quoted: 175,589 km total (2021), 29,579 km paved, 146,010 km unpaved, 827 km controlled-access. Mid is paved plus half the unpaved network (derived midpoint); high is the total.

railKm.note: World Bank 1,639 km (1998, low); CIA Factbook 1,854 km (2017). Isolated lines (Central, Southern), little military value.

majorPorts.note: CIA Factbook 2024: 20 ports, 0 large + 1 medium + 3 small; key ports Callao, Matarani, Talara, Iquitos. The Chancay megaport (opened 2024) is not yet in the Factbook count (high).

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess. Peru is below the 1 million GT threshold of the merchant-fleet table (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_merchant_navy_capacity_by_country); CIA Factbook 2023 counts 111 merchant ships (9 tankers).

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Andean and Amazon terrain; sustainment by air and river.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Horses, donkeys, mules and llamas (pack animals still used in the Andes); not from FAO data.

nuclearWarheads.note: Peru is a non-nuclear-weapon state (NPT); not listed by FAS Status of World Nuclear Forces. Party to Tlatelolco.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.2: Andes, Amazon and coastal desert, population support; high 1.3 for altitude/jungle climates invaders are not adapted to.

notes: Modern snapshot, asOf 2025 data with 2026 order of battle. Population convention: everything inside ne:PER (World Bank). Money in 2011 int$ via derived:ppp-rebase-2011. Force counts: IISS Military Balance 2026 (personnel) as quoted; IISS Military Balance 2024 via the List of equipment of the Peruvian Army; Peruvian Air Force inventory; Peruvian Navy fleet table. Pending procurement (K2 tanks, K808, F-16 Block 70) is NOT in the 2026 order of battle; several contracts were stalled by the 2026 political crisis. ships_major = frigates; ships_minor = corvettes, OPVs, LPD/LST; drones = Group 2+ UAVs. Infantry P-role splits are educated guesses (grade D). National Police (77,000) excluded.
